Only if the referenced table is empty
Yes, unless another constraint such as NOT NULL forbids it
Only if all indexes are removed

Turn all primary keys into NULL

questions.question: For every nontrivial functional dependency X → A, which condition characterizes 3NF?

X and A must both be non-prime
X is a superkey or A is a prime attribute
A must always be a primary key by itself

questions.subject: dbms
questions.question: What condition defines BCNF for functional dependencies?

Every attribute must be a single-column primary key
Every relation must have exactly two columns
Every nontrivial dependency has a superkey as determinant
Every relation must avoid all foreign keys
questions.explanation: In Boyce-Codd Normal Form, the determinant of each nontrivial functional dependency is a superkey. This is stricter than 3NF.

questions.subject: dw_dm
questions.question: For an association rule X → Y, what does support measure?
options: The fraction of X-containing transactions that also contain Y
The fraction of all transactions containing X but not Y
The fraction of transactions containing either X or Y, including those containing just one
The fraction of all transactions containing both X and Y
The ratio of confidence to the overall frequency of Y
questions.explanation: Rule support is the frequency of the combined itemset X and Y among all transactions. Confidence instead conditions on the transactions containing X. No numerical calculation is needed to distinguish the definitions.

options: The fraction of Y-containing transactions that also contain X
The ratio of rule confidence to the overall frequency of Y
The fraction of X-containing transactions that also contain Y
The fraction of all transactions containing Y regardless of X
The fraction of all transactions containing both X and Y
questions.explanation: Confidence estimates the conditional frequency of Y given X. Reversing the rule to Y → X changes the conditioning group and need not produce the same confidence.

questions.question: What does lift greater than one for X → Y indicate in the observed transaction data?

X has been proved to cause Y
Y occurs with X more often than its overall frequency would suggest
The rule necessarily occurs in most transactions
Every transaction containing X must contain Y
questions.explanation: Lift compares rule confidence with the overall frequency of Y. A value above one indicates positive association in the observed data; it does not by itself establish causation, high support or statistical significance.
